heading: From documents to connected knowledge.
narration: Nitanics connects papers and reports for researchers, analysts, students, and technical teams.

heading: Add your sources in the browser.
narration: Upload Markdown, text, or text-based PDFs through the UI. Choose an extraction API provider and follow the job’s progress.

heading: Attach documents in your agent’s chat.
narration: Or open the cloned repository in Claude Code or Codex. Attach complete documents and use the provided prompt. Your local agent creates, validates, and uploads the graph.
points: Attach full documents or local paths

heading: Both routes. One local graph.
narration: Both feed the same graph in Docker, ready to explore.

heading: Discover concepts across sources.
narration: Explore Graph Studio, search concepts, and use Bridges to compare shared entities. Here, the Federal Reserve connects three finance sources.

heading: Return to the original source.
narration: Inspect document roles, then read the original sources. Compare research findings or technical reports, and check AI-generated claims against the evidence.
points: Shared mentions do not prove agreement

heading: Ingest sources. Reuse graph context.
narration: After ingestion, retrieve relevant graph context through MCP. Reusing entities and connections can reduce repeated document reading and input tokens. Initial extraction still uses tokens; savings vary by workload.

heading: Nitanics
narration: Clone Nitanics, start the local app, and add your sources. Your knowledge, connected.
